DIRECTION A — SPLIT TABLE
The phone lies between the two players. Each half belongs to one of them, the opponent's upside down; tap the left of a half to subtract, the right to add. The only chrome is the seam.

Why: it is the gesture every life app has trained into your hands, and your opponent can fix their own total without reaching across the table.
Cost: half the screen is upside down and useless to you, and the phone has to sit on the table to work — awkward if you keep it in your hand.

The two counters are live: tap the halves.

DIRECTION B — PERSONAL LEDGER
The phone stays with you. Both totals read right way up, yours twice the size of theirs, and between them a ledger of the totals this game has passed through.

Why: you are the one holding the phone and the one keeping the record — and the ledger is the thing the app is named after. It also makes visible the life totals we decided to write into the file.
Cost: your opponent cannot reach their own number without you handing the phone over, and it is not the layout their muscle memory expects.

Live too: tap either panel and watch the ledger grow.

SHARED — the same in both directions
How you leave the counter, what arrives in the match form, and where the counter is opened from. Three entry points: the pill inside the match form (the one you asked for), the square beside "Register round 3" on the home hero, and the small icon in the home header for a casual game with no event at all.

Two stand-ins, not decisions:

• The hero's card art is a drawn placeholder — the real screen pulls the deck's art from Scryfall.

• Mana pips are lettered circles here; the app draws the official SVG symbols.

Everything else — colours, type, radii, control heights — is lifted from theme/colors.ts, theme/typography.ts and the real screens.
